scopes.checked_claim: Original #p5.1 and Eqs.(1)–(2) (#S0.E1/#S0.E2) describe a potential-specific oscillating effective-fluid family. The chosen n=3 branch has averaged w_n=1/2. Original #p9.1 explicitly defines f_EDE(a_c)=Omega_phi(a_c)/Omega_tot(a_c); it does not identify that transition fraction with a peak. The sampled initial coordinate is literally phi_i (#p8.m1), whereas the potential and zero initial-derivative assumption use varphi and dot varphi_i (#p5.1/#p7.1). The selected text does not define phi_i=varphi_i/f or Theta_i. Bulk velocity theta_phi in #p7.1 is a separate perturbation variable. Source-specific sound speed, initial modes and the original modified CLASS mapping are required before source-faithful predictions.

limitations: Omega_phi(a) cannot be substituted for the instantaneous total-density fraction. A constant density-normalizer interpretation and any Omega_phi,0-to-X_c conversion are conditional reader conventions until the original implementation fixes their ownership.

For separately conserved positive scalar and aggregate non-scalar densities, 0<F<1 and a common pressure/density convention, an interior stationary fraction requires w_phi=w_other. With w_total=F w_phi+(1-F)w_other, this is equivalent to w_total=w_phi only on that positive two-sector decomposition. For n=3 the conditional relation is y=(a_stat/a_c)^(9/2)=(1+w_other(a_stat))/(1/2-w_other(a_stat)), requiring -1<w_other(a_stat)<1/2 and finite positive y. The denominator vanishes at w_other=1/2; w_other=-1 gives no finite positive y. The relation is implicit for a varying background and does not establish a maximum, a unique peak or a numerical peak fraction; boundaries and a derivative sign change must also be checked.

The cosine argument varphi/f requires compatible units, but the selected letter does not specify physical units or the normalization/domain of sampled phi_i. No field value, angle range or prior bound is inferred from fitted summaries. Early dot varphi_i=0 is a source assumption, not a supplied full initial-mode prescription.

The explicit MontePython footnote URL and CLASS bibliography are navigation witnesses, not an EDE repository/commit/configuration. Original code identity is unresolved within the retained sources, rather than proved globally unavailable.

The reviewer fluid independently chooses X=rho_fluid/rho_crit,ref,0, a nine-halves density shape and compensated Lambda at fixed H0. Its source interface has density_at_transition, transition_scale and ruler_endpoint, with a complete retained thermal reference. These are not source-normalized scalar coordinates or an admitted paper EDE implementation.

The necessary matched ruler has 0<a_end<=1 and a supplied endpoint; it predicts neither drag/decoupling nor thermal history. Zero-amplitude conservation uses the division-free density equation. Physical perturbation, recombination/reionization, lensed observables, likelihood/prior and shared-data conditioning remain separate open gates.
This accepts only located source definitions and explicit closure gaps. It does not promote the candidate, accept a numerical reference or executable request, or establish a CMB/H0 solution.
